newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares buffeted by inflation ill-information.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares buffeted by inflation ill-information.

text.p: Greek shares dropped 1.52 percent on Thursday dissapointed by a smaller-than-expected fall in the May CPI inflation rate and continuing selling pressure on large caps, brokers said.
Stocks shed around 0.5 percent in late trading after CPI inflation was officially announced. It eased to 5.4 percent in May from 5.9 percent in April.
Brokers said the market had been expecting a figure closer to 5.0 percent, based on reports in Greek financial papers.
"The market was taken by surprise because it was led to believe by radio broadcasts and financial press reports that May CPI inflation would have dropped to around 5.1 to 5.2 percent," said a broker.
Rumours on these figures were making the rounds at brokers' offices this morning, he added.
"There was confusion about the inflation figure reported by financial dailies 'Kathimerini' and 'Imerisia' and other news broadcasts," said another broker.
"The market got the crystal ball out today and fell prey to badly sourced leaks even though the 5.4 percent figure is an excellent improvement." he said.
Reuters had reported earlier in the week that May CPI inflation would settle at 5.4-5.3 percent, citing reliable government sources.
The awaited inflation figure between 5.1 and 5.2 percent had been ruled out with 5.4 percent being the most likely outcome, hence the dissapointment.
Other market participants attributed the market's poor performance to selling pressure on large caps ahead of the part-flotation and rights issue of state telecoms OTE this month.

"Investors are cashing in on large caps which produced sizeable gains during this year's rally in order to raise the liquidity needed to participate in OTE's rights issue," said George Dimitriou, analyst at Ergo Securities.
Other analysts said OTE shares were under pressure in order to avoid raising its issue price but things would change after the rights issue was completed.
"It looks like there is a concerted effort mostly by domestic portfolios to keep OTE's price between 6,500 and 7,000 drachmas to maintain the issue price at reasonable levels," said an analyst.
"I expect the market to remain directionless for the coming week or so until OTE completes its rights issue, but thereafter, OTE will lead the next leg of the rally," he added.
The Athens general index lost 1.52 percent or 25.37 points to 1,644.66 from Wednesday's close of 1,670.03.
Turnover was lower at 17.7 billion drachmas on volume of around 4.0 million shares with little block trade activity.
"Low turnover is the result of a combination of less aggressive buying and unwillingness of sellers to mark down their prices," said Ergo's Dimitriou.
Declining stocks beat advancers 171 to 40 with 27 shares unchanged on 238 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,117-1,147. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, closed 60 drachmas lower at 7,140.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted lower at 670.07-712.84. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $80.93-$82.62. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 4,043-4,273 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $16.81-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted lower at 272-305 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
